tests.exercises: metric_tools/metric_kerr algebra (g_mu_nu inverse, sqrt(-det g), dg/dx^i), cons2primsolver for ieos=2 and ieos=12, substep_gr geodesic integration (precession and inclined circular orbit) for gas particles and for sink particles, extern_gr forces
tests.why: 10 assertions, all pass, output is deterministic text identical at 1/2/4 threads. MUST be pinned to OMP_NUM_THREADS=1: 3.16 s at 1 thread, 38.97 s at 2, 166.11 s at 4 (substep_gr forks an OpenMP region per step for one particle). No shortening needed at 1 thread.
graded_files: stdout: the 10 'checking <name> ... [max err = X, tol = Y]' lines
tests.notes: Filter 'Running in openMP on N threads', 'Total memory allocated to arrays' (1.759 vs 1.762 GB at 1 vs 2 threads), 'total wall time', 'total cpu time' and the 'conservative2primitive  0.00 s' benchmark line. test_rn_charged is skipped (needs METRIC=rn, which no SETUP declares). This check has NO external initial condition, so an ic/variant cannot be produced by perturbing an input file - needs a human decision. | upstream reference: src/tests/test_gr.f90 + build/Makefile:1353 (SETUP=testgr, suite selector 'gr')

tests.exercises: GR sink particles: init_metric/prim2consall/get_grforce_all on sinks, get_accel_sink_sink under a Minkowski metric (mass1=0), energy/momentum/angular-momentum conservation over 100 sink-binary orbits
tests.why: norbits = 100 is a literal in test_sink_binary_gr with dt = C_force*dtsinksink, i.e. of order 1e6 steps, and there is no runtime knob. Both 'phantomtest ptmass' and 'phantomtest ptmassgenrel' were killed at 175-180 s having printed only the first 12 assertions. Cannot be brought under three minutes without patching the source.
tests.notes: Shares the SETUP=testgr build with phantomtest-gr, so it costs no extra build. 'make testgr' runs 'phantomtest gr ptmass', so upstream CI does run this; only our 3-minute rule blocks it. | upstream reference: src/tests/test_ptmass.f90:542 test_sink_binary_gr + build/Makefile:1353 (SETUP=testgr, selectors 'ptmass' / 'ptmassgenrel')

tests.exercises: geodesic integration of 10 test particles in the Kerr metric: metric_kerr, metric_tools, extern_gr substepping, no hydro
tests.why: The full official window (tmax=198.69, dtmax=1.9869, 100 dumps, circular orbit at r=10, spin=0) runs in 0.17 s at 1 thread; no shortening needed. 13.7 s at 2 threads (OpenMP overhead with 10 particles), so pin 1 thread.
tests.notes: npart=10. Bit-identical across repeat runs and across 1 vs 2 threads (only the 100-char fileident timestamp differs). Set nfulldump=1. Knobs: orbtype, spin, r, norbits, dumpsperorbit in myrun.setup; tmax/dtmax in myrun.in. The t=0 dump must be frozen and shipped: a second phantomsetup call reads tmax/dtmax back from 9-digit ASCII and the trajectory then differs by 2e-3 relative after 100 dumps. | upstream reference: src/setup/setup_testparticles.f90 (SETUP=gr_testparticles, METRIC=kerr)

tests.exercises: special-relativistic Sod shock tube: cons2prim/cons2primsolver under strong compression, GR force terms in Minkowski, SPH shock capturing with boundary particles
tests.why: Official window tmax=0.20 at nx=256 (175728 particles) would be ~10x this. Shortened to 2 dumps (tmax=0.02) at nx=128 (87936 particles): 41.5 s at 1 thread, 32.5 s at 2. The classic relativistic hydro test and the hardest cons2prim workout in the module.
tests.notes: Bit-identical 1 vs 2 threads (4 differing bytes, all inside the fileident header at offsets 82-87). Blank answers select the default relativistic shock (densleft=10, prleft=13.333, densright=1, prright=1e-6, gamma=5/3). Knobs: nx, tmax, dtmax, smooth_fac in myrun.setup. | upstream reference: src/setup/setup_shock.f90 (SETUP=srshock, METRIC=minkowski)

tests.exercises: special-relativistic spherical blast wave in a periodic box: cons2prim at high Lorentz factor, GR pressure/energy coupling, periodic boundaries
tests.why: Official tmax=0.20 (40 dumps) at npartx=40 (88320 particles); shortened to 4 dumps (tmax=0.02) at the default resolution: 71.5 s at 1 thread, 34.1 s at 2 (this one does scale). Reduce npartx if the budget tightens.
tests.notes: Bit-identical 1 vs 2 threads (5 differing bytes, offsets 81-87, header only). Knobs: npartx, pblast, pmed, boxsize, rblast, smoothfac in myrun.setup; tmax/dtmax in myrun.in. | upstream reference: src/setup/setup_srblast.f90 (SETUP=srblast, METRIC=minkowski, PERIODIC)

tests.exercises: tidal disruption of a polytropic star by a Kerr black hole: metric_kerr, cons2prim with self-gravity, individual timesteps, GR external force on gas
tests.why: With the buildbot flag --np=1000 the official window (tmax=1.016e4, 500 dumps) is affordable; measured on 50 dumps (tmax=1016, 191 timesteps) at 3.4 s / 1 thread, 22.2 s / 2 threads. The window can be extended a long way before the budget bites.
tests.notes: Evolution from a fixed t=0 dump is bit-identical across repeats and 1 vs 2 threads. BUT phantomsetup is NOT reproducible: relax=.true. runs an OpenMP relax_star, and two fresh runs gave t=0 dumps differing by max|dx|=2.9e-9 (3.4e-11 rel) and up to 1e-7 relative on h. relax_star also restarts from a relax1_00010 dump left in the working directory. Freeze and ship myrun_00000/myrun.in/myrun.setup. Setup cost otherwise 26-40 s per phantomsetup call. | upstream reference: src/setup/setup_grtde.f90 (SETUP=grtde, METRIC=kerr, GRAVITY, IND_TIMESTEPS)

tests.exercises: the tabulated (Einstein Toolkit) metric code path metric_et + metric_et_utils + interpolate3D + tmunu2grid, and the only dump that carries the metric and stress-energy arrays (gtt/gxx/gyy/gzz, dxgtt/dxgxx/dxgyy/dxgzz, tmunutt); periodic dust cosmology
tests.why: Official nx=64 gives 262144 particles; at nx=32 (32768 particles) 5 of the 10 official dumps run in 2.7 s at 1 thread, 3.8 s at 2. Cheap, and it is the only affordable check that grades metric/tmunu arrays.
graded_files: myrun_00005 (Phantom binary full dump, includes gtt/gxx/gyy/gzz, dxg*, tmunutt)
tests.notes: Bit-identical 1 vs 2 threads. HAZARD: standalone Phantom never sets metric_et_utils::gridinit, so metric_et returns Minkowski and zero derivatives (metric_et.f90:47 and :121). The check exercises the et plumbing and tmunu2grid, not a curved tabulated metric; say so in the warrant. No external data file is needed - the fallback is analytic. Knobs: nx, rhozero, cs0, ilattice, FLRW_perturb in myrun.setup. | upstream reference: src/setup/setup_flrw.f90 (SETUP=flrw, METRIC=et, PERIODIC)

tests.exercises: relativistic Bondi accretion onto a Schwarzschild black hole with continuous particle injection at the outer boundary and accretion at the horizon: metric_schwarzschild, cons2prim in a strong field, inject_bondi, accretion bookkeeping
tests.why: At the default pmassi=4e-4 the setup makes 637700 particles and could not finish two dumps in 171 s. With pmassi=4e-3 (68698 particles) four of the 360 official dumps run in 37.8 s at 1 thread, 21.8 s at 2.
tests.notes: The ONLY setup in this module whose evolution is thread-dependent: 12 arrays differ between 1 and 2 threads, max 1.5e-14 absolute (5.6e-13 relative on px), because injection/accretion ordering depends on threads. Pointwise still applies but with a ~1e-11 bound, not bit equality. Knob: pmassi, filldomain in myrun.setup; tmax/dtmax in myrun.in. | upstream reference: src/setup/setup_bondiinject.F90 + src/main/bondiexact_gr.f90 (SETUP=grbondi-inject, METRIC=schwarzschild)

tests.exercises: collision of two polytropic stars near a Kerr black hole, GR initial velocity conditions (use_gr_ic), individual timesteps
tests.why: The full official window (tmax=10, dtmax=1, 10 dumps) with --np=1000 (2000 particles total) runs in 0.58 s at 1 thread, 1.9 s at 2. No shortening needed; the window can be lengthened.
tests.notes: Bit-identical 1 vs 2 threads. Same relax_star non-determinism in phantomsetup as grtde (relax=T for both bodies); freeze the t=0 dump. 3 phantomsetup calls cost 31 s. Knobs: np1/np2, mhole, beta, ecc, semi_maj_val, impact_param in myrun.setup. | upstream reference: src/setup/setup_binary_coll.f90 (SETUP=collgr, METRIC=kerr, IND_TIMESTEPS)

tests.exercises: static polytrope evolved with the SR (Minkowski GR) machinery: cons2prim on a smooth hydrostatic star, individual timesteps
tests.why: Official nr=25 gives 65752 particles and tmax=2e4 (200 dumps). At nr=15 (14328 particles) 2 dumps (tmax=200) run in 11.2 s at 1 thread, 8.4 s at 2.
tests.notes: Bit-identical 1 vs 2 threads (3 bytes, header only). No relaxation in this setup, so phantomsetup is cheap (2 s) - but the ASCII round-trip of tmax/dtmax still argues for freezing the t=0 dump. Knob: nr in myrun.setup. | upstream reference: src/setup/setup_srpolytrope.f90 (SETUP=srpolytrope, METRIC=minkowski, IND_TIMESTEPS)

tests.exercises: self-gravitating polytropic star in the GR (Minkowski) framework: cons2prim plus the tree self-gravity path under GR=yes
tests.why: Official np1=100000 (103806 particles), tmax=100. At np1=10000 (10659 particles) 5 dumps run in 1.2 s at 1 thread, 0.9 s at 2. Cheap; window and resolution both have headroom.
graded_files: myrun_00005 (Phantom binary full dump, includes poten)
tests.notes: Bit-identical 1 vs 2 threads. relax=T in the .setup, so the same relax_star non-determinism applies; freeze the t=0 dump. Knobs: np1, Rstar1, Mstar1, iprofile1, relax in myrun.setup. | upstream reference: src/setup/setup_star.f90 (SETUP=grstar, METRIC=minkowski, GRAVITY)

tests.exercises: relativistic Bondi accretion onto a Schwarzschild black hole without injection
tests.why: With default answers (13124 particles, tmax=122.8) phantom aborts at t~8 with 'evolve: Large error in energy conservation : err = 7.425E-01' and 'FATAL ERROR! evolve: Conservation errors too large to continue simulation'. It only runs with I_WILL_NOT_PUBLISH_CRAP=yes or a window under ~8 code units. grbondi-inject covers the same physics and completes.
tests.notes: Also thread-dependent: 12 arrays differ between 1 and 2 threads at up to 2.8e-14 absolute. Excluded in favour of grbondi-inject. | upstream reference: src/setup/setup_bondi.f90 + src/main/bondiexact_gr.f90 (SETUP=grbondi, METRIC=schwarzschild)

tests.exercises: circumbinary disc / TDE in a binary black hole spacetime read from a tabulated trajectory
tests.why: metric_binarybh requires data/binarybh/cbwaves.txt (a black-hole trajectory table from Zenodo record 10841021). The vendored data/binarybh/ contains only a README; metric_binarybh calls fatal() when the file is missing. Licence-bound external data, fetched over the network at runtime.
tests.notes: Not built and not run. Exclude from the module's entrypoints. | upstream reference: src/main/metric_binarybh.f90 + src/setup/setup_grdisc.f90 (SETUP=binarybh, METRIC=binarybh)

tests.exercises: FLRW universe seeded from a CMB power spectrum, et metric path
tests.why: Not built or run in this investigation; it duplicates the et code path that flrw already covers and adds a power-spectrum input path that was not exercised. Revisit only if the human wants a second et check.
tests.notes: Same et stub limitation as flrw (gridinit is never set standalone). | upstream reference: src/setup/setup_flrwpspec.f90 (SETUP=flrwpspec, METRIC=et, PERIODIC)

tests.exercises: radio tidal disruption event, GR=yes with a Minkowski metric
tests.why: The setup block declares no SETUPFILE; it is a moddump (moddump_radiotde.f90) plus inject_sim.f90 path on top of an existing dump. There is no phantomsetup procedure to run with blank answers, so there is no fixed-input test here.
tests.notes: inject_sim.f90 also reads an external simulation dump. | upstream reference: build/Makefile_setups:240 (SETUP=radiotde, METRIC=minkowski)
